blocks.why: Full night in your own bed before the Bogota nightflight — this is the sleep the whole first duty runs on.
Siesta before an 18:30Z report on a 12h05 overnight; leave home at 16:55Z.
Straight to bed on arrival at 02:00 Bogota local — you have been up all night, take it while the body still wants it.
Normal Bogota night; you get one proper night here so use it.
Afternoon sleep before the 17:10 local report — the flight home lands at 11:45 Madrid with your body still on Bogota time.
Home at 13:50 local off a redeye; short nap only, do not let it run past 17:00 or tonight is wrecked.
Anchor sleep back onto Madrid time before five standby days.
Top-up before a 10h standby that can run to 02:00 local and then hand you a duty.
Bed as soon as the standby window closes.
Long afternoon nap — this is the real sleep for tonight's standby and tomorrow's 06:55Z report, because the gap between them is only 6h55.
Only about four hours available before leaving home at 05:20Z; flagged as short, this is why the afternoon nap was not optional.
Short nap on arrival in Boston at 13:30 local; keep it short so you can still sleep tonight.
Boston local night — the last consolidated sleep before an all-night crossing home.
Deep afternoon sleep before a 21:50 local report on a 23:10 departure; wake with an hour in hand for the 30-minute run to the airport.
Home mid-afternoon after a night crossing; three hours to take the edge off, alarm on.
Full night to reset onto Madrid time before the standby block.
Nap before a 21:00-04:00 local standby — assume you will be called.
Sleep straight off the back of standby; blackout blinds, phone on do-not-disturb.
Same again before the second night standby.
Deliberately cut short — you need to be tired enough to go to bed at 19:30 tonight.
Bed at 19:30 local for an 02:45 alarm and an 03:05Z report; two nights of late standby have shifted you, so use that shift instead of fighting it.
Ninety minutes after a four-sector day that started at 02:45 — enough to get through the evening without stealing tonight's sleep.
First of two clear nights at home; this is where you pay back the early.
Day off, normal night, no alarm needed.
Full night before the Dubai sector; report is a civilised 11:20 local.
23:30-07:30 Dubai local is also 21:30-05:30 Madrid — the one window that suits both clocks on a single-night stop.
Short top-up before the 17:10 local report; the flight home lands at 23:30 Madrid.
Home at 01:35 local off Dubai; sleep now because the next 60 hours are the worst of the month.
Treat this as the main sleep for the whole 18-19SEP block — standby ends 02:00Z and the next report is 05:00Z, so there is nothing behind it.
Stay airside or at an airport hotel and grab whatever you can between standby ending and the 05:00Z report — this is not enough and it should be on a fatigue report.
Blackout sleep in the afternoon before a 14h10 all-night duty; you will be flying through 02:00-06:00 body time on this.
Second daytime sleep in a row before another 22:45Z report; curtains shut, no daylight, no phone.
Third daytime sleep — home at 12:05 local, in bed by 12:30, up at 18:15 for the 18:30Z report.
Home at 07:30 after four consecutive nights; sleep first, sort the day out later.
Second sleep the same day to drag the body clock back onto Madrid nights before the Paris turn.
Bank a long one — tomorrow is 15h20 finishing at 06:05 body time.
Even a light doze before the Singapore sector pays for itself; plan your bunk rest for the back half of the flight, not the first break.
In the hotel by 12:35 Singapore local having been up most of the night; sleep the afternoon, then get up and see daylight.
Singapore local night to consolidate — the layover is long enough to be worth it.
Long afternoon sleep before the 21:50 local report; the duty runs 15h20 and lands Madrid at 06:40 local.
Home at 08:45 with the body on Singapore time; sleep the morning but be up by mid-afternoon or you will not sleep tonight.
Night at home to get back on Madrid time before the last Boston pairing.
Two hours on arrival at 15:30 Boston local after a long day; alarm set, then stay up until local bedtime.
22:00-06:00 Boston local — a compromise that keeps you part-way on Madrid time for the early report on the 30th.
Short banked nap on the day off; cheap insurance for tomorrow's 08:55 local report.
Last night down route; up at 06:00 local, leave the hotel 08:25 for the 12:55Z report.
Home just before 02:00 local at the end of the roster — sleep it off properly.

conflicts.statement: On the STBY lines the roster puts a single time in the column headed 'Off Duty' (14:00Z on 05SEP, 18:00Z on 06SEP, 19:00Z on 10/11/18SEP) with a separate duration. I have read those times as the START of the standby window and added the duration; if the column is literal, standby on 05SEP would be 04:00-14:00Z and on 06SEP 12:00-18:00Z, which changes the sleep plan for 05-07SEP and 18-19SEP completely.
options: Confirm with crewing which end of the window the printed time is
If it is the end time, the 06/07SEP and 18/19SEP rest problems below largely disappear and the naps can be dropped
Until confirmed, plan for the earlier start — it is the more conservative reading

conflicts.statement: Standby on 18SEP runs to 02:00Z and the first sector on 19SEP reports at 05:00Z — three hours between finishing one duty and starting the next, and that three hours sits squarely in the 02:00-06:00 window.
options: Ask to be released from the tail end of the 18SEP standby
Ask for the 19SEP DUB early to be given to someone else
Take an airport hotel so the three hours is not eaten by a 95-minute commute
File a fatigue report if you are called out late on the 18th

conflicts.statement: 19SEP through 22SEP is four duties in a row that all cross 02:00-06:00 body time, with roughly 10 hours between each — every recovery sleep has to be taken in Madrid daylight, which is the sleep you get least of.
options: Blackout blinds, earplugs, cool room; treat the 15:00-21:00 local sleep as non-negotiable
Ask for the 19SEP DUB early to be removed so the night block starts fresh
Plan controlled rest on the flight deck where the operator permits it
Warn the operator now that cumulative fatigue over these four duties is likely

conflicts.statement: Standby on 06SEP closes at 00:00Z (02:00 local) and the MAD-BOS report is 06:55Z the same night — 6h55 total, and after a 95-minute commute each way there is barely four hours in bed.
options: Take the long 06SEP afternoon nap as planned
Ask for an early release from the 06SEP standby
Stay near the airport overnight to recover the commute time
Fatigue-report if you are used late on the 6th

conflicts.statement: An 03:05Z report (05:05 local, out of bed at 02:45) follows two consecutive nights of standby that ran to 04:00 and 05:00 local, then a four-sector 11h24 day.
options: Go to bed at 19:30 local on 12SEP and accept a short evening
Cut the 12SEP morning sleep short so you can get to sleep early
Ask for a later 13SEP report if the standbys were used

conflicts.statement: Two separate duties are rostered on 19SEP: off at 12:34Z and back on at 22:35Z. That is 10h01 door-to-door minus two 95-minute commutes, so the useful sleep window is about six and a half hours in the middle of the afternoon.
options: Sleep 16:45-22:15 local and nothing else
Ask crewing to confirm this is intentional and not a double-assignment error
Consider a room near MAD for that afternoon

conflicts.statement: 08SEP has no line on the roster; it is the Boston layover day between CV220 and CV154, and the CV154 line is dated 09SEP even though you leave the hotel at 21:20 local on the 8th. Easy date to get wrong.
options: Confirm the 08SEP rest day at BOS with crewing
Set your alarms in Boston local time, not UTC or Madrid time

conflicts.statement: CV412 appears twice (DXB-MAD on 17SEP and MAD-FCO on 19SEP), as do CV240 and CV379 on different sectors. Times and routings are self-consistent, so I have taken them as printed, but the numbering looks like a roster-build artefact.
options: Check the flight numbers against the ops schedule before the 19th
Ignore if the operator reuses numbers across fleets or days

conflicts.statement: The two Singapore sectors are 15h20 each and both finish inside the 02:00-06:00 body-time window (04:05Z on 25SEP and 05:10Z on 27SEP), with only about 34 hours down route between them.
options: Take the second rest break on each sector so you sleep closest to the landing
Do not try to fully adapt to Singapore on a 34-hour stop — the plan keeps you part-way
Protect the 26SEP afternoon sleep before the 21:50 local report
